newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire puts Rwandan and Ugandan prisoners on show.
newsitem.headline: Zaire puts Rwandan and Ugandan prisoners on show.

text.p: Zaire, fighting on both diplomatic and military fronts, has put two prisoners on show as evidence that Rwandan and Ugandan soldiers have invaded in support of a rebel revolt in the east.

A Zairean army spokesman said the prisoners, shown to journalists in the capital Kinshasa on Friday, would be used as evidence to back a complaint to the U.N. Security Council that it is a victim of foreign aggression.
The spokesman said one of the prisoners was a Ugandan army corporal and the other a Rwandan lieutenant.
In a separate development, a spokesman for ailing and absent President Mobutu Sese Seko restated Zaire's commitment to a military solution by ruling out negotiations with the rebels.
"We refuse to negotiate with puppets," the spokesman told Radio France International after rebel leader Laurent Kabila said talks interested him more than winning more territory.

With the rebels having opened up a new front towards the mineral-producing southern province of Shaba, relief groups say fresh fighting in the east could halt efforts to help several hundred thousand Rwandan Hutu refugees stranded there.

Also, Zaire has told relief agencies they can only fly planes in via the capital Kinshasa. "This would be very time-consuming and costly," U.N. refugee agency UNHCR spokeswoman Pamela O'Toole said in Geneva.
The Tutsi-led rebels launched their offensive in October, accusing Zaire of denying them citizenship and seeking to expel them to Rwanda, which their forebears left generations ago.
Zaire's army, which launched a much-trumpeted counter-offensive on January 20, says it has taken numerous Rwandan and Ugandan soldiers prisoners.

A defence ministry adviser on judicial and humanitarian affairs, a Captain Djoly, told reporters many regular army prisoners from Rwanda and Uganda were in Kisangani, headquarters of the counter-offensive.
"There too we have imprisoned soldiers from the Ugandan and Rwandan armies, as well as Kabila's criminals," he said.
"There are also numerous wounded being held in Kisangani where they are receiving appropriate medical treatment."
The army put on show three men on Friday, saying they had been taken prisoner during fighting in the east in December.
The third was a South African doctor of Zairean origins accused of helping the rebels.
Sub-Lieutenant Alain-Claude Kalisa, the Rwandan, said he was among 3,000 Rwandan army troops operating in Zaire.
"We were told Zaire constituted a threat to Rwanda," he said, adding that Hutu hardliners behind the 1994 Rwanda genocide of minority Tutsis were there and threatened to destabilise Rwanda.
He said he had been wounded in shelling and captured by Zairean soldiers after his unit retreated. He was unable to identify precisely where he was captured on December 29.
The Ugandan, Kenneth Mugisha, speaking Swahili and English, simply said he had been obeying orders.
Zaire says he was captured in the north eastern town of Nia Nia about 250 km (170 miles) from Kisangani.
The doctor said he was working with relief group Medecins Sans Frontieres when he was captured in Nia Nia.
The army put on a more convincing display of captured Rwandans in November, including an officer recognised by journalists from Rwanda's capital Kigali.
